filename: A Turbulence Model for Velocity Distribution in Open-Channel Flows Through Mangrove Trees.pdf
title: A Turbulence Model for Velocity Distribution in Open-Channel Flows Through Mangrove Trees
parameterization_target: turbulent shear stress in vegetated canopy flows
testbed_rationale: The study does not develop machine learning models and validates an analytical/numerical turbulence closure against small sets of 1D profile observations (8 profiles total).
pain_points: Conventional single mixing-length models fail to capture multi-scale turbulent eddy structures created by complex prop root morphology
The spectral velocity model approximates the inertial subrange with canonical Kolmogorov scaling and neglects the canopy drag-induced spectral bump ('von Kármán street' wake production)
Significant sensitivity to drag coefficient (Cd) formulation and uncertainty in measuring root frontal area vertical distributions
extraction_notes: Funded in part by the NSF LEAP STC (award 2019625, S. Li). The paper does not use machine learning; it formulates a physical co-spectral budget (CSB) turbulence closure and derives an approximate analytical solution for velocity profiles.
